findings.F1: The book loses to fees, not to the forecast. Before fees the positions summed to +1.80, but fees summed to 20.77 on a turnover of 19,205. Across 58,401 trades with a median hold of 5 hours, the mean trade made -0.386% before fees and -0.486% after. The book's mean daily return was -0.001116, against +0.00119 for holding the coins.
findings.F2: Most of the turnover is hourly churn, not new signals. Re-sizing inside a position made 10,712 of the 19,205 turnover (56%) and regime flips made 6,157 (32%). Forecasts switching on or off made only 2,336. Only 42% of active forecasts were still active 24 hours later.
findings.F3: The same forecast pays when held at its own horizon. Taking a position only at the 72-hour grid bars and holding it 72 hours gave a Sharpe of 0.48 after fees, with a daily mean of +0.000288 net and +0.000396 gross, against -1.44 for the hourly book.
findings.F4: The rebound sits in the deepest 3-day falls only. The excess 72-hour return was +0.0092 in the deepest tercile (t 2.32, n 608), -0.0059 in the middle tercile (t -1.81, n 609) and -0.0088 in the shallowest (t -3.17, n 608). Deep 3-day falls combined with big 1-day falls gave +0.0133 (n 371).
findings.F5: Inside the active cases, a larger 1-day fall pays and a small one loses. The biggest 1-day-fall tercile earned +0.0076 excess (t 2.03), and the smallest earned -0.0097 (t -3.38). Grid bars with forecasts between 0 and 8 averaged -0.006 to -0.009 excess (n 695), while forecasts from 8 to 21 averaged +0.0013 (n 1,196).
findings.F6: Taken equally weighted, the active grid cases do not beat the coin's average. Their mean excess was -0.0017 (t -0.87, n 1,891), and the edge appears only when weighted by forecast (+0.0027). The weak cases, which come from mild 3-day falls, dilute it.

ideas.idea: When a coin has fallen over the past 3 days, the larger its fall over the last 1 day, the more it rises over the next 3 days, and the deeper its 3-day fall, the larger that rebound.
ideas.consequence: Buy the rebound in proportion to both the depth of the 3-day decline and the size of the fresh 1-day drop, and refuse it after mild 3-day declines where the coin keeps underperforming.
ideas.name: deep decline fresh-drop rebound

ideas.idea: When a coin has fallen over the past 3 days, the larger its fall over the last 1 day, the more it rises over the next 3 days, with the rise building across the whole 3 days rather than in the first hours after the drop.
ideas.consequence: Take the rebound once, when the drop is seen, and hold it for about 3 days rather than re-sizing it hour by hour, so the gain is not spent on fees.
ideas.name: slow three-day rebound hold
